sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **29 of the official questions in Inferences are this one** — 2 Easy, 6 Medium, 21 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The passage lays out a puzzling observation: an odd trait, an unexpected location, a behaviour that doesn't seem to fit.
- Or it sets up an experiment and what the researchers expected.
- The blank follows 'the team hypothesizes that', 'anticipated that ... would' or 'suggesting that'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the surprise, or the pattern the researchers expect to hold or reverse.
- 2) Ask what one explanation or outcome would make every stated detail make sense.
- If the setup says an effect will flip, flip it.
- 3) Choose the option that explains the puzzle using only the details the passage gives you.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick an explanation that sounds scientific but ignores a key detail, such as the setting, the comparison group or the direction of the effect.
Or, in a flipped-effect setup, you choose the original effect instead of its reverse.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
